docs.title: The client in a stored procedure
docs.text: A stored procedure can query another Tarantool instance: the network client runs inside Tarantool as well as outside it. Given tarantool.fiberio.io(), it does its network I/O by yielding the fiber of the procedure instead of blocking the thread, as net.box does in Lua. This page writes such procedures.

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
src/relay.zig:

//! relay: stored procedures that read another instance over iproto.

const std = @import("std");
const t = @import("tarantool");
const client = @import("tarantool-client");

fn connect(uri: []const u8) !client.Connection {
    return client.Connection.connect(std.heap.c_allocator, t.fiberio.io(), .{
        .address = uri,
        // Give up on a dead peer after 2 seconds instead of waiting forever.
        .timeout = .{ .duration = .{
            .raw = .{ .nanoseconds = 2 * std.time.ns_per_s },
            .clock = .awake,
        } },
    });
}

/// relay.count(uri, space) -> the number of tuples in a space of uri.
fn count(uri: []const u8, space: []const u8) !u64 {
    var conn = try connect(uri);
    defer conn.close();
    const name = try std.fmt.allocPrint(t.region.allocator(), "box.space.{s}:count", .{space});
    return conn.call(name, .{}, u64);
}

/// relay.get(uri, key) -> the value of key in the kv space of uri, or nil.
fn get(uri: []const u8, key: []const u8) !?[]const u8 {
    var conn = try connect(uri);
    defer conn.close();
    const row = try conn.space("kv").get(.{key}, struct { []const u8, []const u8 }) orelse return null;
    // The string borrows the buffer of the connection, which close() frees:
    // copy it to the region, where the result is encoded from.
    return try t.region.allocator().dupe(u8, row[1]);
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportProc("count", count);
    t.proc.exportProc("get", get);
}

The instance can query itself, which shows that the procedure yields: while get waits for the reply, the same thread serves the request it sent.

box.cfg{ listen = '127.0.0.1:3302' }
local kv = box.schema.space.create('kv', { if_not_exists = true })
kv:create_index('pk', { parts = { { 1, 'string' } }, if_not_exists = true })
kv:replace({ 'lang', 'zig' })
box.schema.user.grant('guest', 'read', 'space', 'kv', { if_not_exists = true })
box.schema.user.grant('guest', 'execute', 'universe', nil, { if_not_exists = true })

box.schema.func.create('relay.count', { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
box.schema.func.create('relay.get', { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })

box.func['relay.count']:call({ '127.0.0.1:3302', 'kv' })   -- 1
box.func['relay.get']:call({ '127.0.0.1:3302', 'lang' })   -- zig
box.func['relay.get']:call({ '127.0.0.1:3302', 'rust' })   -- nil
box.func['relay.get']:call({ '127.0.0.1:1', 'lang' })      -- error: ConnectionRefused

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
fiberio.io() returns a std.Io that keeps no state. Its sockets are non-blocking: when a read, a write or a connect would block, the fiber waits in coio.wait, and the TX thread runs other fibers until the socket is ready. The client is the same code as in a standalone program; only the io differs.

  • Call it from a fiber. Every stored procedure runs in one, and so does a fiber you spawn. A worker thread of coio.call does not.
  • Only the network is implemented. Connecting to an IP address, reading, writing and closing a socket: what the client needs. Every other operation of std.Io, such as files, timers or async, panics with its name.
  • The address is numeric. As everywhere in the client, host:port takes an IP address; resolve a name with coio.getAddrInfo first.
  • Set a timeout. Without .timeout, a connect to a host that does not answer waits for as long as the operating system does. A refused connect fails at once.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
The procedures above open a connection per call, which costs a round trip of greeting and login each time. A connection can outlive the call, in a global, but it handles one request at a time: two fibers that use it at once mix their requests. Guard a shared connection with a latch, or keep one per fiber.

A connection allocates with the allocator you give it; std.heap.c_allocator works in any fiber. Close a connection in the fiber that uses it.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: A procedure that waits on the network yields, and memtx aborts a transaction that yields unless the instance runs the MVCC engine. Query the other instance before or after a local transaction, not inside it. See Transactions.

docs.title: Decimals and extensions
docs.text: Tarantool stores decimals, UUIDs, datetimes and intervals as MessagePack extensions. The SDK computes with decimals through the C API of Tarantool, and the msgpack module encodes and decodes all four. This page shows both in the module money.

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
src/money.zig:

//! money: decimal arithmetic, and the extension types of Tarantool.

const t = @import("tarantool");
const Decimal = t.decimal.Decimal;
const ext = t.msgpack.ext;

/// money.total(price, qty, tax_percent) -> price * qty * (1 + tax_percent / 100),
/// rounded to cents.
fn total(price: Decimal, qty: u32, tax_percent: Decimal) !Decimal {
    const hundred = Decimal.fromInt(100);
    const one = Decimal.fromInt(1);
    const rate = try (try tax_percent.div(&hundred)).add(&one);
    const amount = try price.mul(&Decimal.fromUint(qty));
    return (try amount.mul(&rate)).round(2);
}

/// money.split(amount, n) -> the share of each of n, rounded down to cents.
fn split(amount: Decimal, n: u32) !Decimal {
    return (try amount.div(&Decimal.fromUint(n))).floor(2);
}

/// money.cents(amount) -> the amount in cents, as an integer.
fn cents(amount: Decimal) !i64 {
    return (try amount.mul(&Decimal.fromInt(100))).toInt();
}

/// money.uuid_version(uuid) -> the version of a UUID.
fn uuidVersion(e: ext.Ext) !u8 {
    const u = try ext.parseUuid(e);
    return u.bytes[6] >> 4;
}

/// money.epoch(datetime) -> its Unix time, in seconds.
fn epoch(e: ext.Ext) !i64 {
    return (try ext.parseDatetime(e)).seconds;
}

/// money.nil_uuid() -> 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
fn nilUuid() ext.Uuid {
    return .{ .bytes = @splat(0) };
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportProc("total", total);
    t.proc.exportProc("split", split);
    t.proc.exportProc("cents", cents);
    t.proc.exportProc("uuid_version", uuidVersion);
    t.proc.exportProc("epoch", epoch);
    t.proc.exportProc("nil_uuid", nilUuid);
}

local decimal = require('decimal')
for _, name in ipairs({ 'total', 'split', 'cents', 'uuid_version', 'epoch', 'nil_uuid' }) do
    box.schema.func.create('money.' .. name, { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
end
local function call(name, ...)
    return box.func['money.' .. name]:call({ ... })
end

call('total', decimal.new('19.99'), 3, decimal.new('20'))   -- 71.96
call('split', decimal.new('100'), 3)                        -- 33.33
call('cents', decimal.new('12.34'))                         -- 1234
call('total', 19.99, 3, decimal.new('20'))                  -- error: NotExt
call('uuid_version', require('uuid').new())                 -- 4
call('epoch', require('datetime').new({ year = 2026, month = 1, day = 1 })) -- 1767225600
call('nil_uuid')                                            -- 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

docs.title: Decimals
docs.text:
tarantool.decimal.Decimal is the decimal of Tarantool, up to 38 digits, with its arithmetic. It is a value: every operation returns a new decimal.

Group Functions Make zero(), fromInt(i64), fromUint(u64), fromFloat(f64), fromString(s) Convert toInt(), toUint(), toString(&buf) Arithmetic add, sub, mul, div, rem, pow, neg, abs Functions sqrt, ln, log10, exp Rounding round(scale), half away from zero; floor(scale), toward zero; rescale(scale); trim() Inspect order(&other), precision(), scale(), isInt(), isNeg()

The binary operations take the other operand by pointer: a.add(&b). A result out of range, a division by zero or a logarithm of a negative fails with error.DecimalError; a string or a float that is no decimal with error.InvalidDecimal; toInt of a decimal too large with error.Overflow.

toString writes into a buffer of decimal.string_buffer_size bytes:

var buf: [t.decimal.string_buffer_size]u8 = undefined;
const text = amount.toString(&buf); // [:0]const u8

A Decimal encodes as the decimal extension, and decodes from it only: a stored procedure that takes one fails on a plain number with NotExt, as the fourth call above does. A Lua function of lua.exportModule takes and returns the decimal of Lua.

Decimal needs Tarantool to compute, so it lives in the tarantool module. msgpack.ext.Decimal, in msgpack, carries the digits of a decimal without computing with them, for the network client: fromString, toString, and it encodes as the extension.

docs.title: UUIDs, datetimes, intervals
docs.text:
msgpack.ext has a type for each extension of Tarantool:

Type Extension Fields ext.Uuid UUID, 2 bytes: [16]u8 ext.Datetime datetime, 4 seconds, nsec, tzoffset in minutes, tzindex ext.Interval interval, 6 year, month, week, day, hour, min, sec, nsec, adjust ext.Decimal decimal, 1 the digits, the scale and the sign ext.Ext any type, the code, and data, the payload

Each of them encodes as its extension. To decode, take an ext.Ext and parse it: ext.parseUuid(e), ext.parseDatetime(e), ext.parseInterval(e), ext.parseDecimal(e). Each fails when the extension is of another type, and e.kind() tells the type. A field of a tuple read with Tuple.field is a msgpack.Value whose .ext holds the same Ext.

docs.title: Fibers
docs.text: This page runs code in fibers of its own from a module: fibers you join, a background fiber you cancel, channels between fibers, a condition variable, and work offloaded to a thread. Fibers and yields explains the model. The module is workers.

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
src/workers.zig:

//! workers: fibers, a channel, a condition variable, and a worker thread.

const std = @import("std");
const t = @import("tarantool");
const fiber = t.fiber;

fn square(x: i64, delay: f64) i64 {
    fiber.sleep(delay);
    return x * x;
}

/// workers.squares(n) -> 1² + ... + n², each square computed in a fiber.
fn squares(n: u32) !i64 {
    var fibers: [16]fiber.Fiber(i64) = undefined;
    if (n > fibers.len) return error.TooMany;
    var spawned: usize = 0;
    errdefer for (fibers[0..spawned]) |f| {
        _ = f.join();
    };
    while (spawned < n) : (spawned += 1) {
        fibers[spawned] = try fiber.spawn("square", square, .{ @as(i64, @intCast(spawned + 1)), 0.01 });
    }
    var sum: i64 = 0;
    for (fibers[0..n]) |f| sum += f.join();
    return sum;
}

fn consume(ch: *fiber.Channel(i64)) i64 {
    var total: i64 = 0;
    while (ch.recv() catch return total) |v| total += v;
    return total;
}

/// workers.pipeline(n) -> 1 + ... + n, sent through a channel of 4 slots to a
/// consumer fiber.
fn pipeline(n: i64) !i64 {
    var ch = try fiber.Channel(i64).init(4, std.heap.c_allocator);
    defer ch.deinit(); // after the join: no fiber waits on it any more
    var consumer = try fiber.spawn("consumer", consume, .{&ch});
    var i: i64 = 1;
    while (i <= n) : (i += 1) try ch.send(i); // waits while the channel is full
    ch.close(); // the consumer takes what is left, then sees the end
    return consumer.join();
}

var ticks: u64 = 0;
var ticker: ?fiber.Fiber(void) = null;

fn tick(counter: *u64) void {
    while (!fiber.isCancelled()) {
        counter.* += 1;
        fiber.sleep(0.01);
    }
}

/// workers.start(): start a fiber that counts ticks until workers.stop().
fn start() !void {
    if (ticker != null) return error.Running;
    ticker = try fiber.spawn("ticker", tick, .{&ticks});
}

/// workers.stop() -> the number of ticks counted.
fn stop() !u64 {
    const f = ticker orelse return error.NotRunning;
    ticker = null;
    f.cancel();
    f.join();
    return ticks;
}

var flag = false;
var flag_cond: ?t.cond.Cond = null;

fn flagCond() !t.cond.Cond {
    if (flag_cond == null) flag_cond = try t.cond.Cond.init();
    return flag_cond.?;
}

fn isSet(f: *bool) bool {
    return f.*;
}

/// workers.wait_flag(timeout) -> true once set_flag ran, false on timeout.
fn waitFlag(timeout: f64) !bool {
    const cond = try flagCond();
    cond.waitUntil(&flag, isSet, timeout) catch |e| switch (e) {
        error.Timeout => return false,
        else => return e,
    };
    return true;
}

/// workers.set_flag(): wake every fiber in wait_flag.
fn setFlag() !void {
    flag = true;
    (try flagCond()).broadcast();
}

const Digest = struct { input: []const u8, out: [32]u8 = undefined };

/// Runs on a worker thread: touches nothing but `d`.
fn digest(d: *Digest) isize {
    std.crypto.hash.sha2.Sha256.hash(d.input, &d.out, .{});
    return 0;
}

/// workers.sha256(s) -> the hex SHA-256 of s, computed on a worker thread.
fn sha256(s: []const u8) ![]const u8 {
    var d: Digest = .{ .input = s };
    _ = try t.coio.call(Digest, digest, &d);
    const hex = std.fmt.bytesToHex(d.out, .lower);
    return t.region.allocator().dupe(u8, &hex);
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportProc("squares", squares);
    t.proc.exportProc("pipeline", pipeline);
    t.proc.exportProc("start", start);
    t.proc.exportProc("stop", stop);
    t.proc.exportProc("wait_flag", waitFlag);
    t.proc.exportProc("set_flag", setFlag);
    t.proc.exportProc("sha256", sha256);
}

for _, name in ipairs({ 'squares', 'pipeline', 'start', 'stop', 'wait_flag',
                        'set_flag', 'sha256' }) do
    box.schema.func.create('workers.' .. name, { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
end
local function call(name, ...)
    return box.func['workers.' .. name]:call({ ... })
end

call('squares', 10)               -- 385
call('pipeline', 100)             -- 5050
call('start')
require('fiber').sleep(0.1)
call('stop') > 5                  -- true
call('wait_flag', 0.05)           -- false
require('fiber').create(function() require('fiber').sleep(0.05) call('set_flag') end)
call('wait_flag', 0.5)            -- true
call('sha256', 'abc')             -- ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad

The timeouts are f64, so they take a float: call('wait_flag', 1) fails with NotFloat, because Lua sends 1 as an integer. See Encoding.

docs.title: Spawn and join
docs.text:
fiber.spawn(name, f, args) creates a fiber that runs f with the tuple args, and returns a fiber.Fiber(R), where R is what f returns. join() waits for the fiber to end and returns that value; it may be an error union. Join each fiber exactly once.

spawn yields: the new fiber runs until its first yield before spawn returns. In squares, each fiber starts, sleeps, and the loop spawns the next one; the ten sleeps overlap.

  • fiber.spawnWithAttr(name, attr, f, args) takes a fiber.FiberAttr, which sets the stack size of the fiber: attr.setStackSize(bytes). Deep recursion, or large arrays on the stack, need more than the default.
  • fiber.spawnDetached(name, f, args) starts a fiber nobody joins; f must return void.
  • A Fiber handle has cancel, wakeup, id, name, setName and csw, the number of context switches. fiber.find(id) looks up any fiber, read only.

The arguments of a fiber must outlive it. In pipeline, the consumer gets a pointer to the channel on the stack of the procedure, which is valid because the procedure joins the consumer before it returns. The ticker gets a pointer to a global, since it outlives the call that starts it.

docs.title: Cancel
docs.text: ticker.cancel() asks the ticker fiber to stop. The fiber sees it at its next yield: fiber.sleep returns early, and fiber.isCancelled() is true. A fiber that waits in Cond.wait, Channel.send or recv gets error.Cancelled instead.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
fiber.Channel(T).init(capacity, alloc) is a bounded queue between fibers; any number of fibers may send and receive.

Method Does send(value) queues value; waits while the channel is full; error.Closed once it is closed recv() takes the oldest value; waits while the channel is empty; null once it is closed and empty close() wakes every waiting fiber; the values queued still arrive deinit() frees the channel; no fiber may wait on it

docs.title: Condition variables and latches
docs.text:
cond.Cond wakes fibers that wait for a condition:

Method Does wait(), waitTimeout(seconds) waits for a signal; error.Timeout, error.Cancelled waitUntil(context, pred, timeout) waits until pred(context) is true, checking it at each wake, within timeout seconds of the call signal(), broadcast() wakes one waiting fiber, or all of them

latch.Latch is a mutex for fibers, for a section of code that yields and must not run in two fibers at once:

const lock = try t.latch.Latch.init();
defer lock.deinit();
lock.lock();
defer lock.unlock();

tryLock() takes it only if it is free, and withLock(context, f) runs f(context) under it. Code that does not yield needs no latch: no other fiber runs in between.

docs.title: Worker threads
docs.text:
coio.call(Ctx, f, &ctx) runs f(&ctx) on a worker thread of Tarantool and yields the fiber until f returns; it returns what f returned. Meanwhile the TX thread serves other requests. f runs outside the TX thread, so it must not call the box, Lua, the fiber region or any fiber function: give it the data it needs in ctx, as sha256 does.

coio.getAddrInfo(host, port, hints, timeout) resolves a name the same way, without blocking the TX thread:

var addrs = try t.coio.getAddrInfo("localhost", "3301", null, 1.0);
defer addrs.deinit();
var it = addrs.iterator();
while (it.next()) |ai| _ = ai; // *std.c.addrinfo

coio.wait(fd, .{ .read = true }, timeout) waits until a non-blocking file descriptor is readable or writable, and coio.close(fd) closes one and wakes the fibers waiting on it.

docs.title: Time
docs.text: fiber.sleep(seconds) sleeps the fiber. fiber.time() and fiber.clock() are the wall-clock and monotonic time of the current event loop iteration, in seconds; time64() and clock64() in microseconds. tarantool.clock reads the system clocks themselves: realtime, monotonic, process and thread, in seconds, and with 64 in nanoseconds.

docs.title: Introspection
docs.text: This page reads the state of the instance from a module: its status, whether it is read-only, its schema version and LSN, the memory of memtx. It also covers the clocks, and reaching functions that Tarantool does not export.

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
src/probe.zig:

//! probe: the state of the instance, as a stored procedure sees it.

const t = @import("tarantool");
const info = t.box.info;

/// probe.state() -> {status = , ro = , schema = , lsn = , arena_used = }
fn state() struct { status: []const u8, ro: bool, schema: u64, lsn: ?i64, arena_used: u64 } {
    return .{
        .status = @tagName(info.status()),
        .ro = info.isRo(),
        .schema = info.schemaVersion(),
        .lsn = info.lsn(),
        .arena_used = info.slab(.arena_used),
    };
}

/// probe.wait_rw(timeout) -> true once the instance is writable, false on timeout.
fn waitRw(timeout: f64) !bool {
    info.waitRo(false, timeout) catch |e| switch (e) {
        error.Timeout => return false,
        error.Cancelled => return e,
    };
    return true;
}

/// probe.has_symbol(name) -> whether the executable has a symbol, exported or not.
fn hasSymbol(name: []const u8) bool {
    return t.symresolve.resolve(name) != null;
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportProc("state", state);
    t.proc.exportProc("wait_rw", waitRw);
    t.proc.exportProc("has_symbol", hasSymbol);
}

for _, name in ipairs({ 'state', 'wait_rw', 'has_symbol' }) do
    box.schema.func.create('probe.' .. name, { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
end
local function call(name, ...)
    return box.func['probe.' .. name]:call({ ... })
end

call('state').status          -- running
call('state').ro              -- false
call('wait_rw', 0.1)          -- true
call('has_symbol', 'txn_begin') -- true

docs.title: The state of the instance
docs.text:
box.info reads what box.info and box.slab.info() show in Lua:

Function Returns status() .running, .loading, .orphan or .hot_standby isRo() whether the instance is read-only roReason() why it is read-only, or null; the string is valid until the next box call waitRo(ro, timeout) waits until the instance is read-only, or writable; error.Timeout, error.Cancelled schemaVersion() the schema version, which every DDL increases lsn() the LSN of this instance in its vclock, or null before the bootstrap slab(what) a figure of box.slab.info(), in bytes: .items_size, .items_used, .arena_size, .arena_used, .quota_size, .quota_used

A replica waits with waitRo(false, timeout) until it becomes the leader before it writes.

docs.title: Clocks
docs.text:
Function Clock fiber.time(), fiber.time64() wall clock, as of the current iteration of the event loop: cheap, and the same for every fiber of the iteration fiber.clock(), fiber.clock64() monotonic, as of the current iteration clock.realtime(), clock.monotonic() the system clocks, read at the call clock.process(), clock.thread() the CPU time of the process, and of the thread

fiber.time64 and fiber.clock64 count microseconds, clock.*64 nanoseconds; the others return seconds as f64.

docs.title: Hidden symbols
docs.text:
The C API of Tarantool, module.h, is a part of what its executable contains. The rest is compiled in too, but not exported: dlsym does not find it, and neither does a module that declares it as extern. symresolve.resolve(name) reads the full symbol table of the executable, and returns the address of the symbol, or null:

const raw = t.symresolve.resolve("txn_begin") orelse return error.NoSymbol;
const txn_begin: *const fn () callconv(.c) ?*anyopaque = @ptrCast(raw);
_ = txn_begin;

Pass the name of the C symbol, without the leading underscore of macOS. The cast is yours: nothing checks that the type matches the function.

This is an escape hatch, not an API. The internal functions of Tarantool have no stable signature, and change between versions; a stripped executable has no symbol table, and nothing resolves. The tarantool/tarantool Docker images keep it; check the build you deploy with has_symbol above.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: A module writes to the log of Tarantool: the destination of box.cfg.log, with its format and its level. tarantool.say does it, and adapts std.log to it, so that the std.log calls of the module and of its dependencies go there too.

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
src/chatty.zig:

//! chatty: log through say, and through std.log.

const std = @import("std");
const t = @import("tarantool");
const say = t.say;

/// Route std.log of this module, and of everything it imports, to the log of
/// Tarantool.
pub const std_options: std.Options = .{ .logFn = say.stdLogFn };

const log = std.log.scoped(.chatty);

/// chatty.hello(name): log at each level.
fn hello(name: []const u8) void {
    say.info("hello, {s}", .{name});
    say.warn("{d} bytes of name", .{name.len});
    if (say.enabled(.debug)) say.debug("debug is on", .{});
    log.info("through std.log", .{});
}

/// chatty.open(path): log the error of a failed open, with its errno.
fn open(path: []const u8) !void {
    const z = try t.region.allocator().dupeSentinel(u8, path, 0);
    const fd = std.c.open(z, .{});
    if (fd < 0) {
        say.sysError(@backingInt(std.c.errno(fd)), "cannot open {s}", .{path});
        return error.OpenFailed;
    }
    _ = std.c.close(fd);
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportProc("hello", hello);
    t.proc.exportProc("open", open);
}

box.schema.func.create('chatty.hello', { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
box.schema.func.create('chatty.open', { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
box.func['chatty.hello']:call({ 'zig' })
pcall(box.func['chatty.open'].call, box.func['chatty.open'], { '/nonexistent' })

I> hello, zig
W> 3 bytes of name
I> (chatty): through std.log
!> cannot open /nonexistent: No such file or directory

Each line starts with the time, the process id, the fiber and the position, as other lines of the log do. The position is zig:0: Zig gives a function no way to know the line that called it, so put what identifies the line in the message.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
Function Level say.err E>, error say.crit C>, critical say.warn W>, warning say.info I>, information say.verbose V>, verbose say.debug D>, debug say.sysError(errno, fmt, args) !>, system error: the message of errno appended

A message above the box.cfg.log_level of the instance is not written, and not formatted: the level is checked first. say.enabled(level) tells whether a level is written, to skip work that only a message needs. The level is read at each call, so a change of box.cfg{log_level = ...} takes effect at once.

The format is that of std.fmt, not of printf. A line is formatted in a buffer of 1024 bytes on the stack; a longer one is cut and ends with ....

docs.title: std.log
docs.text:
say.stdLogFn as the logFn of the std_options of the root source file sends std.log to the log of Tarantool: err, warn, info and debug map to the levels of the same names, and a scope other than the default one prefixes the message, as (chatty): above.

std.log filters by its own level as well, at compile time: std_options.log_level defaults to .debug in a debug build and to .info in the release ones, so a release build has no std.log.debug calls at all, whatever box.cfg.log_level says.

docs.title: Lua modules
docs.text: A module can be a Lua module too: require('geo') loads geo.so and calls its luaopen_geo, which returns a table of functions. lua.exportModule makes that entry point from a struct of Zig functions. This page writes one, with typed functions and a raw one.

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
src/geo.zig:

//! geo: a Lua module of plain Zig functions.

const std = @import("std");
const t = @import("tarantool");
const lua = t.lua;

const Point = struct { lat: f64, lon: f64 };

/// geo.distance(a, b) -> the great-circle distance in km.
fn distance(a: Point, b: Point) f64 {
    const rad = std.math.pi / 180.0;
    const dlat = (b.lat - a.lat) * rad;
    const dlon = (b.lon - a.lon) * rad;
    const h = std.math.pow(f64, @sin(dlat / 2), 2) +
        @cos(a.lat * rad) * @cos(b.lat * rad) * std.math.pow(f64, @sin(dlon / 2), 2);
    return 2 * 6371.0 * std.math.asin(@sqrt(h));
}

/// geo.bounds(points) -> the south-west corner, the north-east corner.
fn bounds(points: []const Point) !lua.Multi(struct { Point, Point }) {
    if (points.len == 0) return error.NoPoints;
    var sw = points[0];
    var ne = points[0];
    for (points[1..]) |p| {
        sw = .{ .lat = @min(sw.lat, p.lat), .lon = @min(sw.lon, p.lon) };
        ne = .{ .lat = @max(ne.lat, p.lat), .lon = @max(ne.lon, p.lon) };
    }
    return lua.multi(.{ sw, ne });
}

/// geo.parse('55.75,37.62') -> {55.75, 37.62}, or nil.
fn parse(s: []const u8) ?struct { f64, f64 } {
    const comma = std.mem.indexOfScalar(u8, s, ',') orelse return null;
    const lat = std.fmt.parseFloat(f64, s[0..comma]) catch return null;
    const lon = std.fmt.parseFloat(f64, s[comma + 1 ..]) catch return null;
    return .{ lat, lon };
}

/// geo.name(tuple) -> field 2 of a box.tuple.
fn name(row: t.box.Tuple) ![]const u8 {
    return (try row.get(1, []const u8, std.heap.c_allocator)) orelse error.NoName;
}

/// geo.nargs(...) -> the number of arguments: a raw lua_CFunction.
fn nargs(L: ?*t.c.lua_State) callconv(.c) c_int {
    const l = lua.Lua.init(L.?);
    l.pushInt64(l.top());
    return 1;
}

comptime {
    lua.exportModule("geo", .{
        .distance = distance,
        .bounds = bounds,
        .parse = parse,
        .name = name,
        .nargs = nargs,
    });
}

local geo = require('geo')

math.floor(geo.distance({ lat = 55.75, lon = 37.62 }, { lat = 59.94, lon = 30.31 })) -- 635
geo.bounds({ { lat = 1, lon = 5 }, { lat = 3, lon = 2 } }) -- {lat = 1, lon = 2}, {lat = 3, lon = 5}
geo.bounds({})                                  -- error: NoPoints
geo.parse('55.75,37.62')                        -- {55.75, 37.62}
geo.parse('north')                              -- nil
geo.name(box.tuple.new({ 7, 'Moscow' }))        -- Moscow
geo.nargs(1, 'a', nil)                          -- 3
geo.distance({ lat = 1 }, { lat = 2, lon = 2 }) -- error: TypeMismatch

exportModule(name, defs) exports luaopen_<name>, which builds a table with one function per field of defs. Lua looks for the module as it does for any C module: geo.so, or geo.dylib on macOS, on package.cpath. A module may export both stored procedures and luaopen_<name>.

docs.title: Typed functions
docs.text:
A field of defs that is a plain Zig function is wrapped: its arguments are read from the Lua stack by the types of its parameters, and its result is pushed back.

Zig parameter Takes bool a boolean f32, f64 a number an integer type a number, or an int64_t or uint64_t cdata, in range; else error.Overflow []const u8 a string, copied to the fiber region []T a table used as an array a tuple struct a table used as an array, one element per field a named struct a table, a key per field ?T nil, or what T takes box.Tuple a box.tuple decimal.Decimal a decimal Zig result Lua value bool, f32, f64 a boolean, a number a signed integer type an int64_t cdata an unsigned integer type a uint64_t cdata []const u8 a string []T, a tuple struct an array table a named struct a table with a key per field ?T nil for null box.Tuple a box.tuple; the wrapper releases the reference you return decimal.Decimal a decimal lua.Multi(struct { A, B }) two values, A and B void nothing
  • The arity is exact. A call with a different number of arguments fails with ArityMismatch, even when the missing ones are optional: pass nil.
  • The types are exact. A string where a number is expected fails with TypeMismatch, and so does a missing key of a named struct whose field is not optional.
  • Integers are 64-bit cdata. They compare equal to Lua numbers: geo.nargs(1, 2) == 2 is true. tonumber() turns one into a number.
  • The fiber region holds the scratch. Strings and arrays taken from Lua, and anything f allocates on the region, live until the function returns; the wrapper restores the region after it pushed the result.
  • Errors are Lua errors. A Zig error returned by f is raised with its name. error.BoxOp is raised with the message of Tarantool, for example Duplicate key exists in unique index "pk".

docs.title: Several results
docs.text:
lua.Multi(T), where T is a tuple struct, returns each field as a value of its own. lua.multi(.{ a, b }) builds one when every element is known at run time only. With a constant element, such as a string literal, declare the type and fill .values:

fn nameAge() lua.Multi(struct { []const u8, i64 }) {
    return .{ .values = .{ "bob", 30 } };
}

A plain tuple struct, without Multi, returns one array table, as parse does.

docs.title: Raw functions
docs.text:
A field of defs whose type is fn (?*c.lua_State) callconv(.c) c_int is registered as it is: a lua_CFunction, which reads its arguments from the Lua stack, pushes its results and returns their number. lua.Lua.init(L.?) wraps the state with the stack operations:

Method Does top(), typeOf(i), pop(n) the number of values, the type of one, pop pushNil, pushBool, pushNumber, pushInt64, pushUint64, pushLString push a value toBool, toNumber, toInt64, toUint64, toLString read a value; none of them raises newTable, getField, setField, rawGetI, rawSetI, objLen tables raise(message) raise a Lua error; it does not return

raise jumps out of the function with longjmp, past any defer of the Zig frames in between. Raise only from the outermost frame of the function, after everything that needs a cleanup has run; lua.raiseErr(l, err) raises a Zig error the way the typed wrapper does.

docs.title: Network client
docs.text: tarantool-client is an iproto connector: a Zig program uses it to work with Tarantool over the network. This page goes through a program that does each kind of request: CRUD, calls, batches, the schema, watchers and a transaction. Your first client sets up a project for it.

docs.title: The server
docs.text:
shop.lua:

require('fio').mktree('data')
box.cfg{
    memtx_dir = 'data',
    wal_dir = 'data',
    listen = '127.0.0.1:3301',
    memtx_use_mvcc_engine = true, -- for the transaction over a stream
}
box.once('shop', function()
    box.schema.user.create('shop', { password = 'secret' })
    box.schema.user.grant('shop', 'read,write,execute', 'universe')
    local products = box.schema.space.create('products', {
        format = {
            { name = 'id', type = 'unsigned' },
            { name = 'name', type = 'string' },
            { name = 'price', type = 'unsigned' },
        },
    })
    products:create_index('pk', { parts = { 'id' } })
    products:create_index('by_name', { parts = { 'name' } })
end)
box.broadcast('price_list', 7)

$ tarantool shop.lua

docs.title: The program
docs.text:
src/shop.zig:

//! shop: every kind of request of tarantool-client, against shop.lua.

const std = @import("std");
const client = @import("tarantool-client");
const msgpack = @import("msgpack");
const update = @import("tarantool-proto").update;

/// A row of `products`: id, name, price.
const Product = struct { u64, []const u8, u64 };

pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void {
    const gpa = init.gpa;
    var conn = try client.Connection.connect(gpa, init.io, .{
        .address = "127.0.0.1:3301",
        .user = "shop",
        .password = "secret",
    });
    defer conn.close();

    // CRUD, by the name of the space. Row = void discards the result.
    const products = conn.space("products");
    _ = try products.replace(.{ 1, "tea", 300 }, void);
    _ = try products.replace(.{ 2, "coffee", 450 }, void);
    _ = try products.replace(.{ 3, "cocoa", 380 }, void);

    const tea = (try products.get(.{1}, Product)).?;
    std.debug.print("get: {s} costs {d}\n", .{ tea[1], tea[2] });

    // Field numbers count from 0: 2 is the price.
    const cheaper = (try products.update(.{2}, .{update.sub(2, 50)}, Product)).?;
    std.debug.print("update: {s} costs {d}\n", .{ cheaper[1], cheaper[2] });

    // A request the server refuses: error.ServerError, details in last_error.
    if (products.insert(.{ 1, "green tea", 320 }, void)) |_| {
        unreachable;
    } else |err| switch (err) {
        error.ServerError => std.debug.print("insert: {s}\n", .{conn.last_error.?.message}),
        else => return err,
    }

    // A secondary index, and a range.
    const cocoa = (try products.index("by_name").get(.{"cocoa"}, Product)).?;
    std.debug.print("by name: cocoa is {d}\n", .{cocoa[0]});
    const from_two = try products.select(gpa, .{2}, .{ .iterator = .ge, .limit = 10 }, Product);
    defer gpa.free(from_two);
    std.debug.print("select: {d} products from id 2\n", .{from_two.len});

    // Calls and evals decode their single result.
    const count = try conn.call("box.space.products:count", .{}, u64);
    const total = try conn.eval("return ... + box.space.products:get(1)[3]", .{100}, u64);
    std.debug.print("call: {d} products; eval: {d}\n", .{ count, total });

    // A batch: three requests, one write, the replies matched to them.
    var batch = conn.batch(gpa);
    defer batch.deinit();
    const h_ping = try batch.ping();
    const h_get = try batch.get(products, .{3});
    const h_count = try batch.call("box.space.products:count", .{});
    try batch.execute();
    try batch.expectOk(h_ping);
    const third = (try batch.decodeMaybe(h_get, Product)).?;
    const n = try batch.decodeOne(h_count, u64);
    std.debug.print("batch: {s}, {d} products\n", .{ third[1], n });

    // The schema: spaces, their formats and indexes, fetched once and cached.
    const schema = try conn.schema();
    const info = schema.space("products").?;
    std.debug.print("schema: products has {d} fields, the second is {s}\n", .{ info.format.len, info.format[1].name });

    // Watchers: the current value once, or every change.
    const version = try conn.watchOnce("price_list", ?i64);
    try conn.watch("price_list");
    const event = try conn.waitEvent(); // the current value comes first
    var dec = msgpack.Decoder.init(event.data.?);
    std.debug.print("watch: {s} = {d}, once: {?d}\n", .{ event.key, try msgpack.decode(i64, &dec), version });

    // An interactive transaction, over a stream of its own.
    var tx = try client.Stream.open(&conn);
    try tx.begin();
    _ = try tx.space("products").replace(.{ 4, "mate", 500 }, void);
    try tx.rollback();
    const mate = try products.get(.{4}, Product);
    std.debug.print("stream: mate after the rollback: {?s}\n", .{if (mate) |m| m[1] else null});
}

$ zig build && ./zig-out/bin/shop
get: tea costs 300
update: coffee costs 400
insert: Duplicate key exists in unique index "pk" in space "products" with old tuple - [1, "tea", 300] and new tuple - [1, "green tea", 320]
by name: cocoa is 3
select: 2 products from id 2
call: 3 products; eval: 400
batch: cocoa, 3 products
schema: products has 3 fields, the second is name
watch: price_list = 7, once: 7
stream: mate after the rollback: null

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
Connection.connect(gpa, io, options) opens a TCP connection, reads the greeting, negotiates the protocol features, and logs in:

Option Default Is .address host:port, with a numeric IPv4 or IPv6 host .user "guest" the user to log in as .password "" its password; a guest with no password skips the login .timeout .none a std.Io.Timeout for the connect

The login uses chap-sha1, the default of Tarantool Community Edition. The server must be Tarantool 3.0 or later: the client names spaces and indexes in its requests, which older servers do not accept, and connect fails with error.UnsupportedServer. conn.hasFeature(feature) tells which features the server negotiated.

gpa backs the buffers of the connection; close() frees them. Call it exactly once.

io does the network operations. In main, it is the init.io of the Zig runtime. Inside Tarantool, it is tarantool.fiberio.io(), see The client in a stored procedure.

docs.title: CRUD
docs.text:
conn.space(name) is a handle for the requests to a space. It does no I/O: the server resolves the name in each request, so a wrong name fails at the first request, with error.ServerError.

Method Returns insert(row, Row), replace(row, Row) the stored tuple as Row get(key, Row) the tuple, or null; error.MoreThanOne if the key matches several delete(key, Row), update(key, ops, Row) the tuple, or null if no tuple has the key upsert(row, ops) nothing: an upsert returns no tuple select(gpa, key, options, Row) a slice of rows, which you free with gpa index(name) a handle with get and select on a secondary index

Row is the type to decode the tuple into, usually a tuple struct, or void to discard it. The update operations are those of tarantool-proto's update, with field numbers from 0, as in Spaces and indexes.

Each method has a raw twin, insertRaw, getRaw, selectRaw, ..., which takes the row or the key as encoded MessagePack and returns the DATA of the reply as MessagePack.

docs.title: Calls and evals
docs.text:
call(name, args, Result) calls a function, eval(expr, args, Result) runs Lua code. args is a tuple, .{ a, b }, encoded as the argument array. Result is the type of the one value the function returns: a function that returns two values fails with error.ArityMismatch; use a tuple struct for a function that returns a table. Result = void ignores the result.

callRaw(name, args_mp) and evalRaw(expr, args_mp) take the arguments as MessagePack, and return all the results as MessagePack.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A request the server refuses fails with error.ServerError. conn.last_error holds the details until the next server error:

Field Is code the error code of Tarantool message its message raw the error stack as MessagePack, if the server sent one

The other errors are about the connection itself: ConnectionClosed, ReadFailed, WriteFailed, ProtocolError. After one of them, close the connection. See Errors.

docs.title: Batches
docs.text:
A connection waits for the reply to each request before it sends the next. A Batch sends many requests in one write and reads all the replies:

  1. conn.batch(gpa) opens one.
  2. insert, replace, delete, get, select, update, upsert, call, eval, ping add a request and return a handle.
  3. execute() sends them and reads the replies.
  4. decodeOne(h, Row), decodeMaybe(h, Row) and decodeMany(h, gpa, Row) decode a reply; expectOk(h) checks one; serverError(h) returns the error of a request that failed, while the others still succeed.
  5. deinit() frees the replies.

A batch runs once. decodeOne decodes the one tuple of a reply, or the one result of a call or an eval: decodeOne(h_count, u64) above.

docs.title: The schema
docs.text:
conn.schema() fetches the spaces and indexes the user can see, and caches them. Each reply carries the schema version of the server; when it changes, the next schema() fetches again. refreshSchema() fetches at once.

const info = schema.space("products").?;     // *const Schema.SpaceInfo
for (info.format) |field| _ = field;         // .name, .type, .is_nullable
const pk = info.index("pk").?;               // .id, .unique, .parts
_ = pk;

client.decodeRow(Row, info, tuple_mp) decodes a tuple into a named struct by the names of the fields in the format, in any order; an optional field of Row takes a missing tail of the tuple as null.

docs.title: Watchers
docs.text:
box.broadcast(key, value) on the server publishes a value; a client watches it:

  • watchOnce(key, Result) reads the current value, as one request.
  • watch(key) subscribes. The server sends the current value at once, and then each new one.
  • waitEvent() waits for the next event; pollEvent() returns one only if it has arrived already. An event has the key and the value as MessagePack, in data, or null if the key has no value.
  • unwatch(key) unsubscribes.

The connection has no thread of its own: events arrive while you call waitEvent, or while a request reads its reply, and wait in a queue.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: client.Stream.open(&conn) opens a stream: requests that share a transaction on the server. begin(), commit() and rollback() drive it, and stream.space(name) is a space handle whose requests belong to the stream. The server needs memtx_use_mvcc_engine = true for a transaction on memtx that spans requests.

docs.title: Lifetimes
docs.text: A decoded string borrows the buffer of the connection, and the next request overwrites it. tea[1] above is valid until the update that follows it. See Lifetimes.

docs.title: Spaces and indexes
docs.text: This page reads and writes a space from stored procedures: by the tuple, through a typed row, by index ranges and cursors. The module is inventory, over a space of items.

docs.title: The space
docs.text:
local items = box.schema.space.create('items', {
    if_not_exists = true,
    format = {
        { name = 'sku', type = 'string' },
        { name = 'name', type = 'string' },
        { name = 'qty', type = 'unsigned' },
    },
})
items:create_index('pk', { parts = { 'sku' }, if_not_exists = true })
items:create_index('by_qty', { parts = { 'qty' }, unique = false, if_not_exists = true })

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
src/inventory.zig:

//! inventory: items {sku, name, qty}, a primary index on sku and a non-unique
//! index by_qty.

const std = @import("std");
const t = @import("tarantool");
const box = t.box;
const update = t.update;
const msgpack = t.msgpack;

/// A row of `items`, field by field in the order of the space format.
const Item = struct { sku: []const u8, name: []const u8, qty: u64 };
const Items = box.Typed(Item);

/// inventory.add(sku, name, qty): insert an item; a duplicate sku fails.
fn add(sku: []const u8, name: []const u8, qty: u64) !void {
    const items = try Items.byName("items");
    try items.insert(.{ .sku = sku, .name = name, .qty = qty });
}

/// inventory.restock(sku, n) -> the new qty.
fn restock(sku: []const u8, n: u64) !u64 {
    const items = try box.Space.byName("items");
    // Field numbers of Space.update count from 0: 2 is qty.
    const row = (try items.update(.{sku}, .{update.add(2, n)})) orelse return error.NoSuchItem;
    defer row.deinit();
    return (try row.get(2, u64, std.heap.c_allocator)).?;
}

/// inventory.take(sku, n) -> the qty left, or the error NotEnough.
fn take(sku: []const u8, n: u64) !u64 {
    const gpa = std.heap.c_allocator;
    const items = try Items.byName("items");
    var it = (try items.get(.{sku}, gpa)) orelse return error.NoSuchItem;
    defer Items.free(it, gpa);
    if (it.qty < n) return error.NotEnough;
    it.qty -= n;
    try items.put(it);
    return it.qty;
}

/// inventory.edit(sku, name, delta): rename, and add delta to qty if it is
/// not 0. The update operations are built at run time.
fn edit(sku: []const u8, name: []const u8, delta: i64) !void {
    var ops = update.Ops.init(std.heap.c_allocator);
    defer ops.deinit();
    try ops.push(update.set(1, name));
    if (delta > 0) try ops.push(update.add(2, delta));
    if (delta < 0) try ops.push(update.sub(2, -delta));
    const items = try box.Space.byName("items");
    try items.updateDiscard(.{sku}, &ops);
}

/// inventory.count_in(sku, name): one more of sku, created with qty 1 if absent.
fn countIn(sku: []const u8, name: []const u8) !void {
    const items = try box.Space.byName("items");
    try items.upsertDiscard(.{ sku, name, 1 }, .{update.add(2, 1)});
}

/// inventory.remove(sku) -> whether there was such an item.
fn remove(sku: []const u8) !bool {
    const items = try box.Space.byName("items");
    const old = (try items.delete(.{sku})) orelse return false;
    old.deinit();
    return true;
}

/// inventory.item(sku) -> the tuple, or nothing. A raw procedure, to return
/// the tuple itself.
fn item(ctx: ?*t.c.box_function_ctx_t, args: [*c]const u8, args_end: [*c]const u8) !c_int {
    var dec = msgpack.Decoder.init(args[0 .. @intFromPtr(args_end) - @intFromPtr(args)]);
    const sku = (try msgpack.decode(struct { []const u8 }, &dec))[0];
    const items = try box.Space.byName("items");
    const row = (try items.get(.{sku})) orelse return 0;
    defer row.deinit();
    return t.proc.returnTuple(ctx, row);
}

/// inventory.below(limit) -> the skus with qty < limit, highest qty first.
fn below(limit: u64) ![]const []const u8 {
    const region = t.region.allocator();
    const by_qty = try (try box.Space.byName("items")).index("by_qty");
    var range = try by_qty.range(Item, .{ .iterator = .lt }, .{limit}, region);
    defer range.deinit();
    var skus: std.ArrayList([]const u8) = .empty;
    while (try range.next()) |row| try skus.append(region, row.sku);
    return skus.items;
}

const Stock = struct { []const u8, u64 };

/// inventory.top(n) -> {{sku, qty}, ...}: the n items with the most stock.
fn top(n: u32) ![]const Stock {
    const region = t.region.allocator();
    const by_qty = try (try box.Space.byName("items")).index("by_qty");
    const rows = try by_qty.top(n, Item, region);
    const out = try region.alloc(Stock, rows.len);
    for (rows, out) |row, *o| o.* = .{ row.sku, row.qty };
    return out;
}

/// inventory.total() -> the sum of qty over all items.
fn total() !u64 {
    const items = try box.Space.byName("items");
    var cursor = try items.primary().cursor(.{ .iterator = .all }, .{});
    defer cursor.deinit();
    var sum: u64 = 0;
    while (try cursor.next()) |row| sum += (try row.get(2, u64, std.heap.c_allocator)).?;
    return sum;
}

/// inventory.stats(limit) -> {items = , below = }: two counts.
fn stats(limit: u64) !struct { items: usize, below: usize } {
    const items = try box.Space.byName("items");
    const by_qty = try items.index("by_qty");
    return .{ .items = try items.primary().len(), .below = try by_qty.count(.lt, .{limit}) };
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportProc("add", add);
    t.proc.exportProc("restock", restock);
    t.proc.exportProc("take", take);
    t.proc.exportProc("edit", edit);
    t.proc.exportProc("count_in", countIn);
    t.proc.exportProc("remove", remove);
    t.proc.exportRaw("item", item);
    t.proc.exportProc("below", below);
    t.proc.exportProc("top", top);
    t.proc.exportProc("total", total);
    t.proc.exportProc("stats", stats);
}

for _, name in ipairs({ 'add', 'restock', 'take', 'edit', 'count_in', 'remove',
                        'item', 'below', 'top', 'total', 'stats' }) do
    box.schema.func.create('inventory.' .. name, { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
end
local function call(name, ...)
    return box.func['inventory.' .. name]:call({ ... })
end

call('add', 'A-1', 'bolt', 10)
call('add', 'B-2', 'nut', 3)
call('restock', 'B-2', 5)       -- 8
call('take', 'A-1', 4)          -- 6
call('take', 'A-1', 100)        -- error: NotEnough
call('edit', 'A-1', 'hex bolt', -1)
call('count_in', 'C-3', 'washer')
call('item', 'A-1')             -- ['A-1', 'hex bolt', 5]
call('below', 6)                -- ['A-1', 'C-3']
call('top', 2)                  -- [['B-2', 8], ['A-1', 5]]
call('total')                   -- 14
call('stats', 6)                -- {items = 3, below = 2}
call('remove', 'C-3')           -- true

docs.title: Spaces
docs.text:
box.Space.byName(name) looks up the id of a space; error.NoSuchSpace if there is none. A Space is the id and nothing else, cheap to copy and keep.

Operation Returns insert(row), replace(row) the stored tuple get(key), delete(key) the tuple, or null update(key, ops) the updated tuple, or null if no tuple has the key upsert(row, ops) null: an upsert returns no tuple to a module insertDiscard, replaceDiscard, deleteDiscard, updateDiscard, upsertDiscard nothing: they release the tuple for you truncate() nothing

A row and a key are tuple structs, .{ sku, name, qty } and .{sku}, or any value that encodes as an array. Every returned tuple holds a reference that deinit releases, see Lifetimes.

A failed operation, such as a duplicate key, returns error.BoxOp, and the message is in t.err.lastError().

docs.title: Update operations
docs.text:
tarantool.update builds the operations of update and upsert:

Constructor Operation set(field, value) =: assign add(field, n), sub(field, n) +, - band, bor, bxor &, \|, ^ insert(field, value) !: insert a field before field delete(field, count) #: delete count fields splice(field, start, len, str) :: replace part of a string

Pass them as a tuple, .{ update.set(1, name), update.add(2, 1) }, or build an update.Ops at run time, as edit does, and pass a pointer to it.

Field numbers count from 0 in Space.update, Index.update and upsert: update.add(2, n) changes the third field, qty. They count from 1 in Tuple.update, which updates a tuple outside a space, as Lua's tuple:update does.

docs.title: Reading a tuple
docs.text:
Method Gives row.get(i, T, alloc) field i, counting from 0, decoded as T; null past the end row.field(i, alloc) field i as a msgpack.Value row.decode(T, alloc) the whole tuple decoded as T, a tuple struct row.decodeRow(Row) the whole tuple decoded into the named struct Row, field by field row.fieldCount(), row.bsize() the number of fields, the size in bytes row.fieldIterator() a cursor over the fields

A string field is a slice of the tuple; see Lifetimes.

docs.title: Typed rows
docs.text:
box.Typed(Row) maps the named struct Row to the tuples of a space, field by field in the order of declaration. The fields of Row may be integers, floats, booleans, enums and []const u8; anything else is a compile error.

Method Does Typed(Row).byName(name) looks up the space put(row) replaces insert(row) inserts; a duplicate key fails with error.BoxOp get(key, alloc) the row, or null; its strings are copied into alloc del(key) deletes Typed(Row).free(row, alloc) frees the strings get copied

take above reads, changes and writes a row. Between the get and the put it does not yield, so no other fiber can change the item in between.

docs.title: Indexes
docs.text:
space.primary() is the primary index; space.index(name) looks one up by name, and space.indexById(id) takes its id.

Method Returns get(key) the tuple, or null min(key), max(key) the first or last tuple with the key; .{} for the whole index count(iterator, key) the number of tuples the iterator visits len(), bsize() the number of tuples, the size of the index in bytes random(seed) a random tuple select(options, key, alloc) a slice of tuples; release each and free the slice iterator(iterator, key) an Iterator, whose next returns tuples you release cursor(options, key) a Cursor, whose next returns tuples it releases range(Row, options, key, alloc) a Range(Row), whose next returns decoded rows with their strings copied top(n, Row, alloc) the n last rows in the order of the index, as a slice update(key, ops) updates through this index extractKey(tuple, alloc) the key of a tuple in this index, as MessagePack

The options are a query.SelectOptions:

.{ .iterator = .ge, .offset = 0, .limit = 10 }

and the iterators are those of Tarantool: .eq, .req, .all, .lt, .le, .ge, .gt, and the bitset and spatial ones. As in Lua, .lt and .le walk the index in descending order: below gets the highest quantities first.

top(n, Row, alloc) is the descending walk of the whole index, .le with an empty key, cut at n rows; free it with Range(Row).freeSlice. below and top allocate on the fiber region, which needs no free.

docs.title: Sequences
docs.text:
tarantool.seq.Sequence advances a sequence of Tarantool:

const ids = try t.seq.Sequence.byName("event_ids");
const id = try ids.next();
try events.insertDiscard(.{ id, name });

next, current, set(value) and reset() are those of box.sequence.<name>. current fails with error.SeqOp on a sequence that never advanced.

docs.title: Key definitions
docs.text:
tarantool.keydef.KeyDef compares tuples by a key that no index has:

const parts = [_]t.keydef.KeyPartDef{
    .{ .fieldno = 2, .type = .unsigned },
    .{ .fieldno = 0, .type = .string },
};
const by_qty_sku = try t.keydef.KeyDef.init(&parts, std.heap.c_allocator);
defer by_qty_sku.deinit();
const order = by_qty_sku.compare(a, b); // std.math.Order

compareWithKey(tuple, key, alloc) compares a tuple with a key, and extractKey(tuple, alloc) cuts the key out of a tuple.

docs.title: Stored procedures
docs.text: A stored procedure of a module is a C function that Tarantool calls as <module>.<symbol>. This page writes procedures with proc.exportProc, which derives the C function from a plain Zig function, and with proc.exportRaw, which leaves the arguments and the results to you. It extends the module of Your first module.

docs.title: Typed procedures
docs.text:
src/procs.zig:

//! procs: the shapes a typed stored procedure can take.

const std = @import("std");
const t = @import("tarantool");

/// procs.clamp(x, lo, hi) -> x limited to [lo, hi], or the error EmptyRange.
fn clamp(x: i64, lo: i64, hi: i64) !i64 {
    if (lo > hi) return error.EmptyRange;
    return std.math.clamp(x, lo, hi);
}

/// procs.parse_u64(s) -> the number, or nil when s is not one.
fn parseU64(s: []const u8) ?u64 {
    return std.fmt.parseInt(u64, s, 10) catch null;
}

const Point = struct { x: i64, y: i64 };

/// procs.mid({x=, y=}, {x=, y=}) -> {x=, y=}: maps in, a map out.
fn mid(a: Point, b: Point) Point {
    return .{ .x = @divTrunc(a.x + b.x, 2), .y = @divTrunc(a.y + b.y, 2) };
}

/// procs.swap({a, b}) -> {b, a}: an array in, an array out.
fn swap(pair: struct { []const u8, []const u8 }) struct { []const u8, []const u8 } {
    return .{ pair[1], pair[0] };
}

/// procs.label(n, unit) -> '<n> <unit>', or '<n>' when unit is nil.
fn label(n: i64, unit: ?[]const u8) ![]const u8 {
    const region = t.region.allocator();
    if (unit) |u| return std.fmt.allocPrint(region, "{d} {s}", .{ n, u });
    return std.fmt.allocPrint(region, "{d}", .{n});
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportProc("clamp", clamp);
    t.proc.exportProc("parse_u64", parseU64);
    t.proc.exportProc("mid", mid);
    t.proc.exportProc("swap", swap);
    t.proc.exportProc("label", label);
}

Each exportProc(name, f) exports a C symbol name that:

  1. decodes the argument array of the call into the parameters of f, by their types, as Encoding lists;
  2. calls f;
  3. encodes the result as the value the call returns, or fails the call with the name of the Zig error that f returned.

The C symbol can differ from the Zig name: parseU64 is exported as parse_u64. Put the exportProc calls in a comptime block of the root source file of the module, or of a file it imports.

docs.title: Declare and call them
docs.text:
for _, name in ipairs({ 'clamp', 'parse_u64', 'mid', 'swap', 'label' }) do
    box.schema.func.create('procs.' .. name, { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
end

local function call(name, ...)
    return box.func['procs.' .. name]:call({ ... })
end

call('clamp', 15, 0, 10)                   -- 10
call('clamp', 1, 10, 0)                    -- error: EmptyRange
call('parse_u64', '42')                    -- 42
call('parse_u64', 'forty-two')             -- nil
call('mid', { x = 0, y = 0 }, { x = 4, y = 2 }) -- {x = 2, y = 1}
call('swap', { 'a', 'b' })                 -- {'b', 'a'}
call('label', 3, 'kg')                     -- '3 kg'
call('label', 3, box.NULL)                 -- '3'

The same functions are callable over the network: conn:call('procs.clamp', {15, 0, 10}) in net.box, conn.call("procs.clamp", .{ 15, 0, 10 }, i64) in the Zig client. A user other than admin needs the right to execute them:

box.schema.user.grant('app', 'execute', 'function', 'procs.clamp')

Creating a language = 'C' function needs execute on universe since Tarantool 3.7.2, 3.8.2 and 3.9.0; create them as admin.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• The arity is exact. A call with fewer or more arguments than f has parameters fails with wrong argument count, and f is not called.
  • An optional parameter still takes an argument. ?T accepts nil, but the nil must be there: in Lua, {3, nil} is a table of one element, so pass box.NULL, as the label call above does.
  • The types are exact. A string where f takes an integer fails with NotInt; an integer where it takes f64 fails with NotFloat. See Encoding.
  • A string argument is borrowed. It is a slice of the request, valid until the procedure returns.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
f returns The call returns a value that value, encoded ?T the value, or nil for null void, !void nothing !T the value, or fails with the error

A procedure returns one value. To return several, or a tuple, write a raw one.

A result allocated on the fiber region, as label does, needs no free: the wrapper encodes it before Tarantool reclaims the region.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: A Zig error returned by a typed procedure fails the call: Tarantool raises a ClientError with code 102, ER_PROC_C, and the name of the error as its message. A box operation that fails returns error.BoxOp, which a typed procedure reports as BoxOp. To keep the message of Tarantool instead, for example Duplicate key exists in unique index "pk", write a raw procedure with exportRaw: it reports error.BoxOp with the error Tarantool set.

docs.title: Raw procedures
docs.text:
A raw procedure has the C signature of a stored procedure: it gets the arguments as a MessagePack array, between args and args_end, and returns its results through ctx. Each proc.returnValue(ctx, value) adds one value to the results; proc.returnTuple(ctx, tuple) adds a tuple.

src/stats.zig:

//! stats.stats(...) -> count, sum, mean of any numbers, integers or floats.

const std = @import("std");
const t = @import("tarantool");
const msgpack = t.msgpack;

fn stats(ctx: ?*t.c.box_function_ctx_t, args: [*c]const u8, args_end: [*c]const u8) !c_int {
    const gpa = std.heap.c_allocator;
    var dec = msgpack.Decoder.init(args[0 .. @intFromPtr(args_end) - @intFromPtr(args)]);
    const all = try dec.decodeValue(gpa);
    defer msgpack.freeValue(gpa, all);

    if (all.array.len == 0) return t.proc.fail(error.NoNumbers, "stats() needs at least one number");

    var sum: f64 = 0;
    for (all.array) |v| sum += switch (v) {
        .uint => |u| @floatFromInt(u),
        .int => |i| @floatFromInt(i),
        .float => |f| f,
        else => return error.NotANumber,
    };
    const n: f64 = @floatFromInt(all.array.len);

    // Three results: each returnValue adds one.
    if (t.proc.returnValue(ctx, all.array.len) != 0) return -1;
    if (t.proc.returnValue(ctx, sum) != 0) return -1;
    return t.proc.returnValue(ctx, sum / n);
}

comptime {
    t.proc.exportRaw("stats", stats);
}

box.schema.func.create('stats.stats', { language = 'C', if_not_exists = true })
box.func['stats.stats']:call({ 1, 2, 4.5 })   -- 3, 7.5, 2.5
box.func['stats.stats']:call({})              -- error: stats() needs at least one number
box.func['stats.stats']:call({ 1, 'two' })    -- error: NotANumber

exportRaw(name, f) exports f, which returns !c_int: 0 on success, or -1 after it set an error. When f returns a Zig error, the wrapper fails the call:

  • with the error Tarantool set, for error.BoxOp;
  • with the name of the error, for any other error.

proc.fail(e, message) does the same with a message of your own and returns -1. To fail with an error code of your choice, set it and return -1:

t.err.setBoxError(t.c.ER_PROC_C, "out of stock");
return -1;

A raw procedure decides how to decode its arguments, so it can take what a typed one cannot: a variable number of arguments, or a value of either type, as stats takes integers and floats as msgpack.Value.
